__meta.what: Golden file for the Reckoning cycle (src/core/time.ts).
__meta.why: The width of the commitment window is an agent-facing rule. If agent.md says "you have N ticks to commit" and the engine allows N-1, that is scar #1 with money on it. The table below is what the engine actually does, so a recalibration shows up as a diff a human reads.
__meta.note_on_width: COMMITMENT_WINDOW_TICKS is 24 and the commitment window is 24 ticks wide (phases 262-285). It USED to be 23, with a note here reasoning that the freeze tick fell inside 'the last 24 ticks' and was excluded - a plausible justification for what was actually an off-by-one, pinned as if intended. A wave-3 verifier found the related defect: inFreeze and isSettlementTick were BOTH true at phase 287, so 'between freeze and settlement' named an empty interval and INV-18 was vacuous in the wired engine. SPEC 5.1 says the freeze is 'the last tick BEFORE settlement', so the four bands are now disjoint and tile the cycle: quiet 0-261, commitment 262-285, freeze 286, settlement 287.
__meta.regenerate: The hand-authored columns are the oracle. To add a case: write it here with a deliberately wrong derived value, run the matching test in test/core, and copy the expected value out of the failure. Never paste engine output in without checking it against arithmetic you did yourself - that turns an oracle into a snapshot of a bug.
